text.p: Following are the main stories from Thursday's Slovenian newspapers.

- Parliament decided that the centre-left Liberal Democrats of Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek will head one of the most important parliamentary committees -- the committee for the election of parliament and government officials.
- U.S. government security advisor Richard Schifter, who visited Slovenia on Wednedsay, said the country could play a significant role in the South European Cooperation Group (SECI).
- Much of Slovenia's industry is technologically outdated and has an inadequate capital stucture, Minister for Economic Activites Metod Dragonja said.
- Slovenia's Smelt Olimpija beat France's Pau Orthez 96-86 in a EuroLeague basketball match on Wednesday.
- The 6th Slovenian film festival started in the port city of Portoroz on Wednesday.
- Slovenian insurance companies are pushing for higher car insurance payments for drivers who repeatedly cause accidents.

- Representatives of unions and employers said they would meet at least once a week until they reach a new general collective agreement on work benefits. The previous agreement expires at the end of May.
- President Milan Kucan met foreign diplomats on Wednesday to mark the 5th anniversary of the recognition of Slovenia's independence by most European countries.
- The British Chamber of Trade started an 18-month campaign to boost trade with member countries of the Central European Free Trade Area (CEFTA), including Slovenia.
- Slovenia's central securities registration body KDD said some companies hesitated to issue shares because they have poor knowledge of markets and securities.
